problems.problem:
N2016-10-4. Algae and Didymosphenia geminata

1.  Read the given text! While reading, choose the correct terms. [1 point for each correct answer; 10 points]

Algae belong to the kingdom <Protista | Monera | Plantae> and use solar energy as a source of energy. Algae are <eukaryotic | prokaryotic> unicellular or multicellular organisms. Algae are found in various environments – mainly in water, but also in soil, on tree bark and on rocks. About 300 000 species of algae are known, and the size of algae can range from a few micrometres to several tens of metres.

Diatoms are mostly unicellular organisms that grow in colonies and whose envelope consists of pectic substances covered by durable siliceous caps. The development of these caps requires <silicon dioxide | potassium sulfate | calcium carbonate | carbon dioxide>.

Brown algae are multicellular organisms that are found almost without exception only in seas – mainly in <tropical | temperate climate zone | cold> seas. They grow attached to the bottom or to other algae. One of the brown algae is also often washed ashore on the coast of the Baltic Sea – <bladderwrack (Fucus vesiculosus) | kelp (Laminaria) | Cladophora>.

Red algae, on the other hand, can be of various forms – both microscopic and macroscopic. They are found mainly in seas and grow attached to a substrate. Red algae are widely used – <gelatin | agar | biofuel | starch> is obtained from them.

Green algae are characterised by a great diversity of forms - they are unicellular, colonial and multicellular organisms. Green algae are distributed all over the world. They grow mainly in <rivers | seas | fresh waters>. Green algae include Volvox, Chlorella, Spirogyra and Chlamydomonas. Both green algae and other algae can be used for <bioindication | insulin production | soil purification | determination of the nitrogen level>.

<Protozoa | Cyanobacteria | Bifidobacteria>, which cause “water bloom”, used to be classed with the algae (blue-green algae). Now they are no longer regarded as algae, because their structure is more similar to bacteria and completely different from the structure of other chlorophyll-containing organisms. Blue-green algae are found in various environments, including both fresh waters and saline waters. They differ from other bacteria in the ability <to carry out photosynthesis | to reproduce sexually | to ferment milk | to grow under anaerobic conditions>. Some species contain several toxins that are potentially dangerous to the health of both humans and the inhabitants of waters.

Didymosphenia geminata (Didymo) is a microscopic unicellular alga (Fig. 23; A) found in fast-flowing, shallow and moderately shallow rivers, especially so-called “salmon rivers”. It can also be observed on lake shores with a rocky substrate exposed to wave action. The proliferation of Didymo is not caused by pollution or excessive phosphorus inflow. On the contrary, waters with a low nutrient content are better suited to Didymo. The outer walls of the algal cell consist of quartz. Didymo has a mucilaginous stalk by which the cells attach to stones and sometimes also to vegetation. During a “bloom” these stalks form mats that cover the river bed. The stalks are not alive and consist of mucopolysaccharides; their colour varies from white to brownish yellow. When touched, the algae resemble wet cotton wool. Didymo cells attach very easily to various surfaces and can survive outside the river in moist conditions for up to 30 days.

Since the mid-1980s the appearance of Didymo has been reported in several countries, especially in the central regions of Canada and in many western US states. In Europe the appearance of Didymo has been confirmed in Finland, Hungary, Ireland, Iceland, Norway, Poland and Romania. A Didymo “bloom” has also been observed in the rivers of the South Island of New Zealand, where the alga has been officially recognised as an unwanted organism. In the map of Figure 23 B the potential distribution ranges of the alga are marked in red.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig23.png

Figure 23. Micrograph of Didymosphenia geminata (A) and its possible distribution range (B; in red).

It is believed that in extreme cases Didymo can affect the river food web, reducing algal diversity and changing the species composition of invertebrates. Didymo stimulates the proliferation of several species of snails, sludge worms, caddisflies and midges and causes a decrease in mayflies. There is reason to believe that changes in physical conditions and in the composition of benthic invertebrate communities could potentially affect the diet of fish. Algal mats in the beds of large rivers can also cause changes in the current. One of the most important effects caused by Didymo is its possible influence on the pH of the environment, which may affect individual organisms or certain developmental stages that are sensitive to environmental pH.

The question of the effect of this alga on salmonid fish is currently topical. One study shows that water polluted with Didymo does not affect the viability of Atlantic salmon spermatozoa, but significantly shortens the duration of spermatozoa activity and causes disturbances in their functioning. These effects could be related to the high polyphenol content in the algae and the possible release of polyphenols into the water. Therefore the spread of Didymo could strongly affect salmonid populations.

2.  Several statements about the alga Didymosphenia geminata are given below. Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 11 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Didymo belongs to the diatoms.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Didymo is characterised by growth in colonies.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Didymo is a benthic organism.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{One of the factors limiting the distribution of the alga might be the mean temperature of the river water.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{In river water Didymo covers a large surface area, therefore its “mats” can serve as an attachment surface for other algae.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Angling and boating on rivers that are polluted with Didymo do not affect its spread.} &  \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{In Latvia the spread of the alga could start first in the Daugava and the Lielupe.} &  \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{If Didymo spread in Latvia, the deposits formed by the alga on the stones of the river bed could hinder the migration of lampreys.} &  \\ \hline \text{9.} & \text{The spread of Didymo could be stopped completely by banning the export of fish and other freshwater organisms from countries in whose rivers the alga has spread.} &  \\ \hline \text{10.} & \text{It is known that the compounds released by the alga affect the motility of spermatozoa, therefore it is possible that these compounds inhibit the function of mitochondria.} &  \\ \hline \text{11.} & \text{The change in environmental pH caused by this alga could negatively affect the development of fish eggs and frog tadpoles.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

3.  The alga Didymo forms various kinds of interaction with its living environment and the organisms inhabiting it. Several statements about the possible influence of Didymo are given below. Choose the interaction that corresponds to each statement. [1 point for each correct answer; 8 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Choose the correct answer from the options offered!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{It is known that substances released by Didymo reduce the motility of spermatozoa, therefore the proliferation of these algae <will decrease | will not affect | will increase> the populations of beavers and otters.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{The inflow of wastewater rich in phosphorus and nitrogen into a river <will promote | will not affect | will reduce> the reproduction of the Didymo population.} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Covering the areas affected by Didymo with a dark film opaque to sunlight <will promote | will not affect | will restrict> the reproduction of the Didymo population.} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{A rapid rise in the mean air temperature by several degrees <will promote | will not affect | will reduce> the spread of Didymo in the rivers of the temperate climate zone.} \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{A ban on wading into rivers in which this alga has spread and on moving along them by boat <will promote | will not affect | will hinder> its spread.} \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{The spread of Didymo <could increase | its effect cannot be determined | could decrease> the potential food sources of some fish species, for example perch, roach and pike.} \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{The effect of a high oxygen level on the alga Didymo in a body of water is most likely <favourable | neutral | unfavourable>.} \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{The migration of waterbirds <promotes | hinders | does not affect> the spread of Didymo.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Source: Olivares, Pamela, Paola Orellana, Guillermo Guerra, Matías Peredo-Parada, Viviana Chavez, Alfredo Ramirez, and Jorge Parodi. 2015. Aquatic Toxicology 163 (June): 102–8. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aquatox.2015.03.022.
problems.problem_orig:
N2016-10-4. Aļģes un Didymosphenia geminata

1.  Iepazīsties ar doto tekstu! Lasīšanas laikā izvēlies pareizos jēdzienus. [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 10 p.]

Aļģes pieder pie <protistu | monēru | augu> valsts un par enerģijas avotu izmanto Saules enerģiju. Aļģes ir <eikariotiski | prokariotiski> vienšūnas vai daudzšūnu organismi. Aļģes sastopamas dažādās vidēs – galvenokārt ūdenī, bet arī augsnē, uz koku mizām, uz klintīm. Zināms apmēram 300 000 aļģu sugu, un aļģu izmēri var būt no dažiem mikrometriem līdz pat vairākiem desmitiem metru.

Kramaļģes lielākoties ir vienšūnas organismi, kas aug kolonijās un kuru apvalks sastāv no pektīnvielām, ko sedz izturīgi krama vāciņi. Šo vāciņu attīstībai nepieciešams <silīcija dioksīds | kālija sulfāts | kalcija karbonāts | ogļskābā gāze>.

Brūnaļģes ir daudzšūnu organismi, kas gandrīz bez izņēmumiem ir sastopami tikai jūrās – galvenokārt <tropiskajās | mērenās klimata zonas | aukstajās> jūrās. Tās aug, piestiprinājušās pie grunts vai citām aļģēm. Arī Baltijas jūras krastā bieži tiek izskalota viena no brūnaļģēm – <pūšļu fuks | laminārija | kladofora>.

Toties sārtaļģes var būt dažādu formu – gan mikroskopiskas, gan makroskopiskas. Tās sastopamas galvenokārt jūrās un aug, piestiprinoties pie substrāta. Sārtaļģes tiek plaši pielietotas – no tām iegūst <želatīnu | agaru | biodegvielu | cieti>.

Zaļaļģēm ir raksturīga liela formu daudzveidība - tās ir gan vienšūnu, gan koloniāli, gan daudzšūnu organismi. Zaļaļģes ir izplatītas visā pasaulē. Tās aug galvenokārt <upēs | jūrās | saldūdeņos>. Pie zaļaļģēm pieder volvoksi, hlorellas, spirogīras, hlamidomonas. Gan zaļaļģes, gan citas aļģes var izmantot <bioindikācijai | insulīna ražošanai| augsnes attīrīšanai | slāpekļa līmeņa noteikšanai>.

<Protozojus | cianobaktērijas | bifidobaktērijas>, kas izraisa “ūdens ziedēšanu”, agrāk pieskaitīja pie aļģēm (zilaļģēm). Tagad tos/tās vairs neuzskata par aļģēm, jo to uzbūve vairāk līdzinās baktērijām un tie/tās pilnīgi atšķiras no citu hlorofilu saturošo organismu uzbūves. Zilaļģes sastopamas dažādās vidēs, tostarp gan saldūdeņos, gan sāļūdeņos. Savukārt no citām baktērijām tās atšķiras ar spēju <veikt fotosintēzi | vairoties dzimumiski | raudzēt pienu | augt anaerobos apstākļos>. Dažas sugas satur vairākus toksīnus, kas ir potenciāli bīstami gan cilvēku, gan ūdeņu iemītnieku veselībai.

Didymosphenia geminata (Didymo) ir mikroskopiska vienšūnas aļģe (23. att.; A), kas sastopama straujās, seklās un vidēji seklās upēs, īpaši t.s. “lašupēs”. To var novērot arī ezeru krastos ar akmeņainu substrātu, kas pakļauts viļņu darbībai. Didymo savairošanos neizraisa piesārņojums vai pārmērīgs fosfora pieplūdums. Tieši pretēji, Didymo labāk ir piemēroti ūdeņi ar zemu barības vielu saturu. Aļģes šūnas ārējās sienas sastāv no kvarca. Didymo ir gļotu kātiņš, ar kura palīdzību šūnas piesaistās pie akmeņiem un dažkārt arī veģetācijas. “Ziedēšanas” laikā šie kātiņi veido paklājiņus, kas pārklāj upes gultni. Kātiņi nav dzīvi un sastāv no mukopolisaharīdiem, to krāsa variē no baltas līdz brūni dzeltenai. Ja tām pieskaras, aļģes atgādina slapju vati. Didymo šūnas ļoti viegli pieķeras dažādām virsmām un ārpus upes mitros apstākļos var izdzīvot pat līdz 30 dienām.

Kopš 1980. gadu vidus par Didymo parādīšanos ziņots vairākās valstīs, īpaši Kanādas centrālajos reģionos un daudzos ASV Rietumu štatos. Eiropā Didymo parādīšanās ir apstiprināta Somijā, Ungārijā, Īrijā, Islandē, Norvēģijā, Polijā un Rumānijā. Arī Jaunzēlandes Dienvidsalas upēs ir novērota Didymo “ziedēšana”, un tur aļģe ir oficiāli atzīta par nevēlamo organismu. 23. attēla B kartē ar sarkano krāsu iezīmēti aļģes potenciālie izplatības areāli.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig23.png

23. att. Didymosphenia geminata mikrofotogrāfija (A) un tās iespējamais izplatības areāls (B; sarkanā krāsā).

Uzskata, ka galējos gadījumos Didymo var ietekmēt upes barošanās tīklu, samazinot aļģu daudzveidību un mainot bezmugurkaulnieku sugu sastāvu. Dydimo stimulē vairāku gliemežu, dūņu tārpu, maksteņu, knišļu sugu savairošanos un izraisa viendienīšu samazināšanos. Ir pamats uzskatīt, ka fizisko apstākļu un bentisko bezmugurkaulnieku sabiedrību sastāva pārmaiņas varētu potenciāli ietekmēt zivju uzturu. Aļģu paklāji lielo upju gultnēs var izraisīt arī pārmaiņas straumē. Viens no svarīgākajiem Didymo izraisītajiem efektiem ir iespējamā tās ietekme uz vides pH, kas var ietekmēt atsevišķus organismus vai noteiktas to attīstības stadijas, kas ir jutīgas pret vides pH.

Šobrīd aktuāls ir jautājums par šīs aļģes ietekmi uz lašveidīgajām zivīm. Viens pētījums liecina, ka ar Didymo piesārņots ūdens neietekmē Atlantijas laša spermatozoīdu dzīvotspēju, bet būtiski saīsina spermatozoīdu aktivitātes ilgumu un izraisa to funkcionēšanas traucējumus. Šie efekti varētu būt saistīti augsto polifenolu saturu aļģēs un polifenolu iespējamo izdalīšanos ūdenī. Tādēļ Didymo izplatīšanās varētu stipri ietekmēt lašveidīgo zivju populācijas.

2.  Zemāk doti vairāki apgalvojumi par aļģi Didymosphenia geminata. Novērtē apgalvojumu patiesumu (P – patiess; A - aplams)! [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 11 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Apgalvojums} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Didymo pieder pie kramaļģēm.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Didymo raksturīga augšana kolonijās.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Didymo ir bentisks organisms.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Viens no aļģes izplatību ierobežojošiem faktoriem varētu būt upes ūdens vidējā temperatūra.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Upes ūdenī Didymo pārklāj lielu virsmas laukumu, tādēļ tās “paklājiņi” var kalpot par pieķeršanās virsmu citām aļģēm.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Makšķerēšana un braukšana ar laivām pa upēm, kuras ir piesārņotas ar Didymo, neietekmē tās izplatību.} &  \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{Latvijā aļģes izplatība vispirms varētu sākties Daugavā un Lielupē.} &  \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{Ja Didymo izplatītos Latvijā, aļģes radītie nogulumi uz akmeņiem upes gultnē varētu traucēt nēģu migrāciju.} &  \\ \hline \text{9.} & \text{Didymo izplatību varētu pilnīgi apturēt, aizliedzot eksportēt zivis un citus saldūdens organismus no valstīm, kuru upēs aļģe ir izplatījusies.} &  \\ \hline \text{10.} & \text{Zināms, ka aļģes izdalītie savienojumi ietekmē spermatozoīdu kustīgumu, tādēļ iespējams, ka šie savienojumi kavē mitohondriju darbību.} &  \\ \hline \text{11.} & \text{Šīs aļģes izraisītā vides pH maiņa varētu negatīvi ietekmēt zivju ikru un varžu kurkuļu attīstību.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

3.  Aļģe Didymo veido dažāda veida mijiedarbību ar dzīves vidi un tajā mītošajiem organismiem. Zemāk doti vairāki apgalvojumi par iespējamo Didymo ietekmi. Izvēlies katram apgalvojumam atbilstošo mijiedarbību. [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 8 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Izvēlies pareizo atbildi no piedāvātajiem variantiem!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Zināms, ka Didymo izdalītās vielas samazina spermatozoīdu kustīgumu, tāpēc šo aļģu savairošanās <samazinās | neietekmēs | palielinās> bebru un ūdru populāciju.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Ar fosforu un slāpekli bagātu notekūdeņu ieplūšana upē <veicinās | neietekmēs | samazinās> Didymo populācijas vairošanos.} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Didymo skarto teritoriju pārsegšana ar tumšu, saules gaismu necaurlaidīgu plēvi <veicinās | neietekmēs | ierobežos> Didymo populācijas vairošanos.} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Strauja gaisa vidējās temperatūras celšanās par vairākiem grādiem <veicinās | neietekmēs | samazinās> Didymo izplatīšanos mērenās klimatiskās zonas upēs.} \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Liegums kāpt upēs, kurās izplatījusies šī aļģe, un pārvietoties pa tām ar laivām <veicinās | neietekmēs | kavēs> tās izplatīšanos.} \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Didymo izplatīšanās <varētu palielināt | ietekme nav nosakāma | varētu samazināt> dažu zivju sugu, piemēram, asaru, raudu, līdaku, iespējamos barības avotus.} \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{Augsts skābekļa līmeņa ietekme uz Didymo aļģi ūdenstilpē, visticamāk, <ir labvēlīga | ir neitrāla | ir nelabvēlīga>.} \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{Ūdensputnu migrācija <veicina | kavē | neietekmē> Didymo izplatīšanos.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Avots: Olivares, Pamela, Paola Orellana, Guillermo Guerra, Matías Peredo-Parada, Viviana Chavez, Alfredo Ramirez, and Jorge Parodi. 2015. Aquatic Toxicology 163 (June): 102–8. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aquatox.2015.03.022.

problems.problem:
N2016-10-5. Urinary system, urine and water homeostasis

1.  Several statements about the kidneys and the urinary system are given. Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 10 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P / A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Urea is formed in the kidneys.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{The primary urine of a healthy person may contain erythrocytes and proteins.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{The urine of patients with diabetes mellitus may contain glucose, and with the help of the kidneys the body reduces the amount of glucose in the blood.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{If 125 ml of primary urine is formed in the kidneys in one minute, then 250 l of primary urine is formed in a day.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{In the capillary tufts, or glomeruli, of the nephron the blood pressure exceeds the osmotic pressure in the blood plasma, ensuring the process of filtration and the formation of primary urine.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Secretion is the transport of substances from the nephron tubules to the capillaries.} &  \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{Antidiuretic hormone reduces the reabsorption of water from the nephron tubules.} &  \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{A human has two urethras and one ureter.} &  \\ \hline \text{9.} & \text{Men suffer from bladder inflammation, or cystitis, more often than women, because the path of the infectious agent through the urinary system to the bladder is shorter in men than in women.} &  \\ \hline \text{10.} & \text{If the volume of urine produced in the kidneys increases, the volume of fluid in the circulation decreases and therefore blood pressure falls.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

2.  Urine tests are often used to characterise the general condition of the human body and to determine specific compounds. Below are named compounds / groups of compounds / particles that can be detected in urine tests. Mark with X which compounds must be present in the urine of a healthy person and which compounds indicate health disorders! [1 point for each correct answer; 7 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|c|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Compound / substance / particles} & \text{Present in the urine of a healthy person} & \text{Present in the urine in case of health disorders} & \text{Never present in the urine} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Glucose} &  &  &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Proteins, for example haemoglobin} &  &  &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \mathrm{Na^+} &  &  &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Microorganisms} &  &  &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Leukocytes} &  &  &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Water} &  &  &  \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{Trichinella worms} &  &  &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig24.png

Figure 24. Microscopic analysis of urine samples. All images are at the same scale.

3.  Urine is also examined microscopically. Figure 24 shows several urine samples that looked cloudy, so a microscopic analysis of them was carried out. Five patients on whom microscopic urine analysis was performed are described below. For each patient indicate the designation of the corresponding urine micrograph (A–D). If no micrograph corresponds to the patient described, write X in the table. [1 point for each correct answer; 5 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Patient description} & \text{Designation in Fig. 24} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{A man with inflammation of the prostate.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{A woman with bladder inflammation (cystitis) caused by a bacterial infection.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{A woman with candidiasis. Candida are yeast-like fungi that, when the immune system is weakened, can grow into mucous membranes.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{A healthy woman.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{A man with liver dysfunction that causes an elevated bilirubin level in the blood.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Urine tests are also often used to determine the level of sex hormones. Several easy-to-use tests are currently available that allow the amount of various hormones in the urine to be determined. Antibodies that bind specifically to a particular hormone are placed on a specially treated strip. If such binding has taken place, the colour of the strip changes. Figure 25 shows the fluctuations in the level of female hormones during the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig25.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): Menstruācija → Menstruation; Folikula nobriešana → Follicle maturation; Ovulācija → Ovulation; Sekrēcijas fāze → Secretory phase; Relatīvā hormona koncentrācija → Relative hormone concentration; ESTROGĒNS → ESTROGEN; PROGESTERONS → PROGESTERONE; Grūtniecības nedēļas → Weeks of pregnancy; Estrogēns → Estrogen; Progesterons → Progesterone

Figure 25. Fluctuations of hormone levels in the urine during the menstrual cycle (A) and pregnancy (B).

4.  Study Figure 25 and answer the questions about hormones in urine tests! [1 point for each correct answer; 5 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Which hormone can be used to determine ovulation by urine tests?} & \text{a. Luteinising hormone (LH); b. Estrogen; c. Progesterone; d. Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Which hormone can be used to detect pregnancy by urine tests?} & \text{a. Estrogen; b. Progesterone; c. Human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG); d. Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Based on the data of graph B, it can be concluded that the onset of pregnancy can be reliably detected with urine test strips:} & \text{a. immediately after intercourse; b. in the second week of pregnancy; c. in the fourth week of pregnancy; d. only in the first two weeks after fertilisation} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Fluctuations in the level of which hormone can be used to predict the onset of menstruation?} & \text{a. luteinising hormone (LH); b. estrogen; c. progesterone; d. follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)} \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Weeks of pregnancy are marked on graph B. From which moment are the weeks of pregnancy counted?} & \text{a. From the moment of fertilisation; b. From the moment of the last intercourse; c. From the moment of the last menstruation; d. From the moment of the last ovulation} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

The human body maintains a certain fluid balance. Table 4 gives data on the amount of water taken in and excreted in the course of a day by an adult man in the temperate climate zone.

Table 4. Daily fluid balance of an adult man in the temperate climate zone.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|l|c|}\hline \text{Source of water taken in} & \text{Volume, ml} & \text{Water excreted with:} & \text{Volume, ml} \\ \hline \text{Metabolic processes} & \text{250} & \text{Faeces} & \text{100} \\ \hline \text{Food} & \text{750} & \text{Sweat} & \text{200} \\ \hline \text{Drinks} & \text{1500} & \text{Evaporation from the lungs and insensible evaporation from the skin} & \text{700} \\ \hline  &  & \text{Urine} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

5.  Study Table 4 and complete the tasks! [1 point for each correct answer; 4 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Write or choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{What volume of water does this person excrete with urine in the course of a day?} & \text{____ ml} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{What proportion of the volume of water taken in during the day is released in the human metabolic processes?} & \text{____ \%} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{During active physical exertion the loss of water significantly increases with:} & \text{a. faeces; b. sweat; c. evaporation from the lungs; d. urine} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Why does this item increase?} & \text{a. Heat energy is produced during muscle activity and must be removed from the body; b. Water is consumed to drive the muscle contraction mechanism; c. Exercise promotes intestinal peristalsis; d. Lactic acid produced in the muscles is excreted with urine} \\ \hline \end{array}$$
problems.problem_orig:

N2016-11-1. Plant tissues and seed germination

1.  Just like animals, plants are multicellular organisms and certain groups of their cells are specialised for performing particular functions. Such groups of cells with a similar structure and function are called tissues. Study Figure 26 and complete the tasks! [1 point for each correct answer; 10 points]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig26.png

Fruit; b. Leaf; c. Root; d. Stem} \\ \hline \text{9.} & \text{To which plant class does the plant shown in Figure 26 belong? a. Monocotyledons; b. Dicotyledons; c. Angiosperms; d. Gymnosperms; e. On a cold December day Ingmārs noticed an unusual phenomenon in the kitchen sink – a small plant had grown in the sink drain (Figure 27). Ingmārs concluded that a seed from some vegetable salad had germinated there, having got stuck in the drain after washing the dishes. Although plant seeds contain reserves of nutrients that provide the seedling with energy and raw materials for forming new structures at the beginning of growth, several environmental factors are also needed for seed germination.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig27.png

Figure 27. Ingmārs’s new flatmate.

2.  In the table mark with X which of the listed environmental factors were available in Ingmārs’s kitchen and are necessary for the seed that fell into the sink to be able to germinate. [1 point for each correct answer; 6 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Environmental factor} & \text{Necessary for germination} & \text{Not necessary for germination} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Moisture} &  &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Light} &  &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{A substrate to grow in} &  &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Air} &  &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Soil as a source of mineral substances} &  &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Warmth} &  &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

3.  Read the text! While reading, choose the correct terms! [1 point for each correct answer; 4 points]

Although plants do not have such well-developed sense organs as animals do, they are able to sense various stimuli and react to them by adjusting their growth. For example, the plant found in the sink, like most other above-ground parts of plants, grows upwards. This phenomenon is called <negative | neutral | positive> <autotrophy | phototropism | gravitropism | thigmotropism>. The leaves of the same plant are turned towards the only window in Ingmārs’s kitchen – this phenomenon is called <negative | neutral | positive> <autotrophy | phototropism | gravitropism | thigmotropism>.

4.  While washing the dishes, Ingmārs accidentally injured the plant, so a break remained 2 cm from the apex. Ingmārs was afraid that the plant would die, but after a couple of days it had grown in length. Ingmārs observed that the distance (stem length) from the edge of the sink to the break had not increased, but the distance from the break to the apex had increased. Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 4 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{The plant’s growth in length takes place throughout the whole stem.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Growth in length can take place by cell division.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{The growth in length has taken place with the help of the apical meristem.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{These observations of Ingmārs provide no information about growth in thickness.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

For plant seeds to germinate successfully, they need certain environmental factors and must be able to resist various factors that may hinder seed germination. The sensitivity of seeds to various environmental conditions can be assessed by measuring seed germination rate (the proportion (%) of sown seeds that germinate). Table 5 summarises the results of an experiment in which the seeds of three different plants were placed in pure water (control) or in solutions of various substances. All other conditions were kept constant during the experiment.

Table 5. Germination rate of the seeds of three different plants (No. 1 – No. 3) under the influence of various stimuli. * The smoke solution in water was prepared by bubbling, for 45 minutes, smoke produced by burning a mixture of various plant materials through a column of water.

In 1996 American scientists observed how the use of additional testosterone affects muscle mass and strength in volunteer men aged 19 to 40 years. The participants of the study used either testosterone or placebo for 10 weeks. During the study some of the participants did not train, while the other part trained in weightlifting. The results of the study are summarised in Table 6 and Figure 29. The value given in the table and the graphs is the arithmetic mean ± standard deviation calculated for all participants of each group (n=13).

The P values given in the graphs characterise how statistically significantly the observed increase differs from the value of the same characteristic of the same group at the start of the experiment. The smaller the P value, the greater the statistical significance of the observed difference. If no P value is given, the observed changes are not statistically significant. An asterisk marks changes that differed statistically significantly from the corresponding group that did not train. A dagger marks changes that differed statistically significantly from the untrained placebo group. A double dagger marks changes that differed statistically significantly from all other study groups.

5.  Read the text! Choose the correct terms. [1 point for each correct answer; 6 points]

The results of the described study show that the testosterone level in the blood can be significantly increased <both by training and by using testosterone preparations | by using testosterone preparations | by using only placebo | only by training>. The use of testosterone without training statistically significantly <does not affect | increases | decreases> the muscle mass of men. Testosterone statistically significantly increases <the serum epitestosterone level | physical strength | the rate of cartilage growth>. It should be noted that by training it is possible to achieve <a small | a statistically insignificant | a statistically significant> increase in muscle strength compared with the placebo group without training. The increase in muscle strength achieved by training alone is similar to the increase in strength after <the use of placebo without training | the use of testosterone with training | the use of testosterone without training>. The use of testosterone can have several side effects, but testosterone therapy does not usually cause <delayed absorption of amino acids in the digestive tract | sexual dysfunction | mood changes | acne (pimples) | shrinking of the testicles>.

5.  Iepazīsties ar tekstu! Izvēlies pareizos jēdzienus. [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 6 p.]

Aprakstītā pētījuma rezultāti liecina, ka testosterona līmeni asinīs ir iespējams nozīmīgi palielināt, <gan trenējoties, gan lietojot testosterona preparātus | lietojot testosterona preparātus | lietojot tikai placebo | tikai trenējoties>. Testosterona lietošana bez treniņa statistiski nozīmīgi <neietekmē | palielina | samazina> vīriešu muskuļu masu. Testosterons statistiski nozīmīgi palielina <epitestosterona līmeni serumā | fizisko spēku | skrimšļa augšanas ātrumu>. Jāatzīmē, ka trenējoties iespējams sasniegt <nelielu | statistiski nenozīmīgu | statistiski nozīmīgu> muskuļu spēka pieaugumu salīdzinājumā ar placebo grupu bez treniņiem. Tikai ar treniņu panāktais muskuļu spēka pieaugums ir līdzīgs spēka pieaugumam pēc <placebo lietošanas bez treniņiem | testosterona lietošanas ar treniņiem | testosterona lietošanas bez treniņiem>. Testosterona lietošanai var būt vairākas blakusparādības, taču testosterona terapija parasti neizraisa <aminoskābju uzsūkšanās aizkavēšanu gremošanas traktā | dzimumdziņas traucējumus | garastāvokļa pārmaiņas | pinnes (akni) | sēklinieku samazināšanos>.

Avots: Bhasin, S., T. W. Storer, N. Berman, C. Callegari, B. Clevenger, J. Phillips, T. J. Bunnell, R. Tricker, A. Shirazi, and R. Casaburi. 1996. The New England Journal of Medicine 335 (1): 1–7. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199607043350101.

problems.problem:
N2016-11-3. Lichens and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fixation

1.  Read the text! Choose the correct terms. [1 point for each correct answer; 11 points]

Lichens are formed by several organisms that are mutually <amensally | parasitically | symbiotically> dependent. Regardless of the appearance, size and location of the lichen, it contains at least one <autotrophic | heterotrophic | organotrophic | parasitic> organism, also called the photobiont. The photobiont may belong to the kingdoms <Monera or plants | Monera or protists | protists or plants | protists or animals>. At present lichens are classified in the kingdom of <plants | animals | Monera | protists | fungi>. Depending on structural features, fruticose, foliose and <cavity | crustose | cushion | bud> lichens are distinguished. Lichens <have | do not have | usually do not have | sometimes have> differentiated tissues, therefore their body is called a <tree | crust (crustose body) | shrub | thallus>. Lichens take up water <from the soil | from the air | from the substrate>. Water uptake takes place <over the whole body surface | through leaves | through roots | through branches>. Because of this physiological feature they are especially sensitive to <soil pollution | air pollution | water pollution>, therefore they can be used as <bioindicators | smoke detectors | oxygen producers | heavy metal filters>.

Lichens can both bind (fix) and release $\mathrm{CO_2}$. The characteristic curves of these two processes in the reindeer lichen Cladonia rangiferina, depending on chlorophyll a content, are shown in Figure 30.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig30.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): ātrums [nmol.s-1.g-1 sausnes] → rate [nmol.s-1.g-1 dry mass]; a hlorofila saturs [µmol.g-1 sausnes] → chlorophyll a content [µmol.g-1 dry mass]; CO2 fiksēšana → CO2 fixation; CO2 izdalīšana → CO2 release

Figure 30. Rate of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fixation and release [nmol.s-1.g-1 dry mass] depending on chlorophyll a content [μmol.g-1 dry mass] in the lichen C. rangiferina.

2.  Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 6 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \mathrm{CO_2}\text{ release can also be called respiration.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Growth of a lichen is possible if it contains at least 2 μmol of chlorophyll a per gram of dry mass.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{The fungus in the lichen is able both to photosynthesise and to respire.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{The amount of }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ fixed in the lichen is greater than the amount of }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ released by the lichen.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{If a lichen contains 2.5 mmol of chlorophyll a per kilogram of dry mass, the amount of }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ it releases will be about two times greater than the amount of }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ fixed.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{From the graph data it can be concluded that if the dry mass of the lichen is 2 g and it contains 3 μmol of chlorophyll a, it can bind at least 50 nmol of }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ in one second.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Lichens are also found in harsh habitats poor in nutrients, for example Buellia grisea grows under the sands of the Ross Desert in Antarctica. Scientists took a soil sample containing a lichen (Fig. 31), kept it at various temperatures (from -10 °C to +15 °C) and illuminated it with light of various intensities (from 100 to 1500 units [U]). It is known that only about 10% of the light reaches the lichen through the topsoil. The scientists also determined the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ absorption rate of the soil sample in the dark (0 U). The results of the study are summarised in Figure 32.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig31.png

Figure 31. Sample of arctic soil with the lichen Buellia grisea (the violet zone indicated by arrows). The scale bar is 5 mm. Image from [10].

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig32.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): CO2 absorbcijas ātrums [mg CO2.dm-2.h-1] → CO2 absorption rate [mg CO2.dm-2.h-1]; temperatūra [oC] → temperature [°C]

Figure 32. $\mathrm{CO_2}$ absorption rate in arctic soil [mg CO2.dm-2.h-1] depending on ambient temperature and illumination.

3.  Answer the questions about the soil samples from the Ross Desert. To make the interpretation of the data easier, we recommend comparing them with the data obtained on $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fixation and release in C. rangiferina (Fig. 30). [1 point for each correct answer; 4 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{A negative }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorption rate in the graph <is a measurement error | indicates }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ release | indicates }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ fixation>.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{A positive }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorption rate in the graph <is a measurement error | indicates }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ release | indicates }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ fixation>.} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{In the described experiment the }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorption rate in the dark characterises <the total respiration of the soil sample | the total respiration and photosynthesis of the soil sample | the total respiration of the lichen | the total photosynthesis of the lichen>.} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{In the described experiment the }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorption rate in the light characterises <the total respiration of the soil sample | the total respiration and photosynthesis of the soil sample | the total respiration of the lichen | the total photosynthesis of the lichen>.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

4.  Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 5 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{When the sun shines on the Ross Desert in Antarctica, the soil is locally thawed and various microorganisms begin to respire.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{The higher the temperature, the better photosynthesis in the arctic desert soil compensates for the respiration of the soil microorganisms.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{In the Ross Desert, biomass growth during the arctic day takes place independently of the ambient temperature.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{To increase the productivity of the Ross Desert soil (the amount of carbon fixed per unit of time), saprophytic organisms should additionally be introduced into the soil.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{The topsoil protects the lichen from UV radiation.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Source: graphs adapted from: Nash, III, Thomas H., ed. 2008. Lichen Biology. 2nd ed. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511790478.

Source: Friedmann, E. Imre, and Henry J. Sun. 2005. Microbial Ecology 49 (4): 523–27. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00248-005-3680-4.

N2016-11-3. Ķērpji un $\mathrm{CO_2}$ saistīšana

1.  Iepazīsties ar tekstu! Izvēlies pareizos jēdzienus. [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 11 p.]

Ķērpi veido vairāki, savstarpēji <amensāliski | parazītiski | simbiotiski> atkarīgi organismi. Neatkarīgi no ķērpja izskata, izmēra un atrašanās vietas tā sastāvā ir vismaz viens <autotrofs | heterotrofs | organotrofs | parazītisks> organisms, ko sauc arī par fotobiontu. Fotobionts var piederēt pie <monēru vai augu | monēru vai protistu | protistu vai augu | protistu vai dzīvnieku> valstīm. Pašlaik ķērpjus pieskaita pie <augu | dzīvnieku | monēru | protistu | sēņu> valsts. Atkarībā no uzbūves īpatnībām, izšķir krūmu, lapu un <dobumu | krevu | pumpiņu | pumpuru> ķērpjus. Ķērpjiem <ir | nav | parasti nav | reizēm ir> diferencēti audi, tāpēc to ķermeni sauc par <koku | krevi | krūmu | laponi>. Ķērpji ūdeni uzņem <no augsnes | no gaisa | no substrāta>. Ūdens uzņemšana notiek <ar visu ķermeņa virsmu | caur lapām | caur saknēm | caur zariem>. Šīs fizioloģiskās īpatnības dēļ tie ir īpaši jutīgi pret <augsnes piesārņojumu | gaisa piesārņojumu | ūdens piesārņojumu>, tāpēc tos var izmantot par <bioindikatoriem | dūmu detektoriem | skābekļa ražotājiem | smago metālu filtriem>.

Ķērpji $\mathrm{CO_2}$ spēj gan saistīt (fiksēt), gan izdalīt. Šo divu procesu raksturlīknes briežu ķērpī Cladonia rangiferina atkarībā no a hlorofila satura redzamas 30. attēlā.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig30.png

30. att. $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fiksēšanas un izdalīšanas ātrums [nmol.s-1.g-1 sausās masas jeb sausnes] atkarībā no a hlorofila satura [μmol.g-1 sausnes] ķērpī C. rangiferina.

2.  Novērtē apgalvojumu patiesumu (P – patiess; A – aplams)! [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 6 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Apgalvojums} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \mathrm{CO_2}\text{ izdalīšanu var saukt arī par elpošanu.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Ķērpja augšana iespējama, ja tas satur vismaz 2 μmol a hlorofila uz gramu sausnes.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Ķērpja sastāvā esošā sēne spēj gan fotosintezēt, gan elpot.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Ķērpī fiksētais }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ daudzums ir lielāks nekā ķērpja izdalītais }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ daudzums.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Ja ķērpis satur 2,5 mmol a hlorofila uz kilogramu sausnes, tā izdalītais }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ daudzums būs apmēram divas reizes lielāks nekā fiksētais }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ daudzums.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{No grafika datiem var secināt, ka tad, ja ķērpja sausne ir 2 g un tajā ir 3 μmol a hlorofila, tas vienā sekundē spēj saistīt vismaz 50 nmol }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Ķērpji ir sastopami arī skarbās, ar barības vielām nabadzīgās dzīvotnēs, piemēram, Buellia grisea aug zem Rosa tuksneša smiltīm Antarktīdā. Zinātnieki paņēma augsnes paraugu, kas saturēja ķērpi (31. att.), turēja to dažādās temperatūrās (no -10 °C līdz +15 °C) un apgaismoja ar dažādas intensitātes gaismu (no 100 līdz 1500 vienībām [U]). Zināms, ka cauri augsnes virskārtai ķērpi sasniedz tikai apmēram 10% gaismas. Zinātnieki noteica arī augsnes parauga $\mathrm{CO_2}$ absorbcijas ātrumu tumsā (0 U). Pētījuma rezultāti ir apkopoti 32. attēlā.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig31.png

31. att. Arktiskās augsnes paraugs ar ķērpi Buellia grisea (violetā zona, kas norādīta ar bultiņām). Izmēra nogrieznis ir 5 mm. Attēls no [10].

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig32.png

32. att. $\mathrm{CO_2}$ absorbcijas ātrums arktiskajā augsnē [mg CO2.dm-2.h-1] atkarībā no vides temperatūras un apgaismojuma.

3.  Atbildi uz jautājumiem par Rosa tuksneša augsnes paraugiem. Datu interpretācijas atvieglošanai iesakām tos salīdzināt ar datiem, kas iegūti par $\mathrm{CO_2}$ fiksēšanu un izdalīšanu C. rangiferina (30. att.). [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 4 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Izvēlies pareizo atbildi!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Negatīvs }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorbcijas ātrums grafikā <ir mērīšanas kļūda | liecina par }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ izdalīšanu | liecina par }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ saistīšanu>.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Pozitīvs }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorbcijas ātrums grafikā <ir mērīšanas kļūda | liecina par }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ izdalīšanu | liecina par }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ saistīšanu>.} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Aprakstītajā eksperimentā }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorbcijas ātrums tumsā raksturo <augsnes parauga kopējo elpošanu | augsnes parauga kopējo elpošanu un fotosintēzi | ķērpja kopējo elpošanu | ķērpja kopējo fotosintēzi>.} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Aprakstītajā eksperimentā }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ absorbcijas ātrums gaismā raksturo <augsnes parauga kopējo elpošanu | augsnes parauga kopējo elpošanu un fotosintēzi | ķērpja kopējo elpošanu | ķērpja kopējo fotosintēzi>.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

4.  Novērtē apgalvojumu patiesumu (P – patiess; A - aplams)! [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 5 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Apgalvojums} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Saulei apspīdot Rosa tuksnesi Antarktīdā, lokāli tiek atkausēta augsne un sāk elpot dažādi mikroorganismi.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Jo augstāka ir temperatūra, jo labāk fotosintēze arktiskā tuksneša augsnē kompensē augsnes mikroorganismu elpošanu.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Rosa tuksnesī biomasas augšana arktiskajā dienā notiek neatkarīgi no vides temperatūras.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Lai paaugstinātu Rosa tuksneša augsnes produktivitāti (saistītā oglekļa daudzumu laika vienībā), augsnē papildus vajadzētu ievadīt saprofītiskus organismus.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Augsnes virskārta pasargā ķērpi no UV starojuma.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

problems.problem:
N2016-11-4. Endangered coral populations

1.  Read the text! Choose the correct terms. [1 point for each correct answer; 9 points]

Corals are colonial organisms consisting of many genetically identical <dicotyledons | flatworms | crustaceans | coelenterates (cnidarians)>. Each coral individual is surrounded by a hard <CaCl2 | CaCO3 | Fe2O3 | SiO2> shell. Corals can reproduce both sexually and asexually. When reproducing <asexually | sexually>, the organisms at the end of a coral "branch" bud and a new genetically identical organism separates from it. In the case of <asexual | sexual> reproduction corals release sperm cells and egg cells into the water. When an egg cell is fertilised, a floating organism arises that is able to form a new coral colony. Many colonial corals form coral stands, which are usually called <nurseries | forests | herds | reefs>. They have <high | negligible | low> biological diversity, therefore they are protected areas. Most coral stands are found in the <Arctic | Atlantic | temperate | tropical and subtropical> climatic zone.

Recently news appeared in the press that the Great Barrier Reef had been declared dead. This news was based on discoveries about “coral bleaching”. In corals living in colonies, symbiotic algae live in the inner cell layer. The symbiotic algae supply the coral with <mineral substances | inorganic substances | organic substances>, which they produce by means of <respiration | filtration | photosynthesis>. At night the coral unfolds its tentacles and catches plankton. Part of the nutrients in the plankton is given to the symbiotic algae. The colour of the coral is given by the algal pigments. Under adverse conditions the symbiotic algae disappear from the coral and it turns white, which is why this phenomenon is called “coral bleaching”. The adverse conditions that can cause “coral bleaching” are increased water temperature, chemical pollution and infections. If the adverse conditions are short-lived, the coral is able to regain the symbiotic algae. For a long time without the symbiotic algae the coral cannot live and dies.

2.  Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 4 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Coral stands are found only in shallow water, where sunlight can reach them.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Widespread coral bleaching is observed in years in which El Niño is pronounced.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Symbiotic algae are not necessary for colony-forming corals to maintain life processes.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{The Great Barrier Reef is not exposed to coral bleaching.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Scientists wanted to assess the benefit that symbiotic algae provide to the coral. For this purpose the water was saturated with labelled $\mathrm{CO_2}$, and the flow of carbon in the coral was followed. The results obtained in the study are shown in Figure 33.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig33.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): Simbiotiskās aļģes → Symbiotic algae; Fotosintēze 250 → Photosynthesis 250; Ar noķerto barību 25 → With captured food 25; Korallim 225 → To the coral 225; Augšanai 0,2 → For growth 0.2; Elpošanai 25 → For respiration 25; Korallis → Coral; Elpošana 100 → Respiration 100; Zudumi ar glotām 98 → Losses with mucus 98; Kaļķa apvalkam 50 → For the calcareous shell 50; Augšanai 2 → For growth 2

Figure 33. Carbon flow in the coral; the number indicates the amount of labelled carbon in milligrams.

3.  Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 6 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Without symbiotic algae corals cannot obtain carbon.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Both the coral and the symbiotic algae allocate less than 1\% of the carbon taken up to growth processes.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{The algae and the coral spend an equal share of the carbon taken up on respiration.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{In the process of respiration carbon leaves the organism in the form of }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Organisms respire in order to convert the nutrients taken up into energy.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{The slow growth of corals can be explained by their carbon balance.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Coral stands are threatened not only by coral bleaching but also by other factors, for example cyclones and the proliferation of predatory starfish. Table 7 summarises the results of several studies on the effect of various harmful factors on coral populations.

Table 7. Coral populations in different geographical locations before and after the action of factors threatening corals.

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Type of damage} & \text{Location} & \text{Coral cover before damage, \%} & \text{Coral cover after damage, \%} & \text{Duration of observations, years} \\ \hline \text{Coral bleaching} & \text{Arabian Gulf} & \text{90} & \text{22–26} & \text{3} \\ \hline  & \text{Coast of Kenya} & \text{26} & \text{23} & \text{5} \\ \hline  & \text{Coast of Tanzania} & \text{33} & \text{0–3} & \text{6} \\ \hline  & \text{Seychelles} & \text{29–64} & \text{0–10} & \text{1} \\ \hline  & \text{Chagos Islands, Indian Ocean} & \text{25–35} & \text{7–33} & \text{8} \\ \hline  & \text{Japan} & \text{95} & \text{0} & \text{2} \\ \hline  & \text{Great Barrier Reef, Australia} & \text{39–63} & \text{9–45} & \text{<1} \\ \hline \text{Proliferation of crown-of-thorns starfish (Acanthaster planci)} & \text{Japan} & \text{80} & \text{0} & \text{2} \\ \hline  & \text{Samoa Islands, Pacific Ocean} & \text{70} & \text{57} & \text{9} \\ \hline  & \text{French Polynesia, Pacific Ocean} & \text{36} & \text{20} & \text{1} \\ \hline \text{Cyclone} & \text{Great Barrier Reef, Australia} & \text{85} & \text{5} & \text{4} \\ \hline  & \text{Tuvalu Islands, Pacific Ocean} & \text{4–93} & \text{1–54} & \text{3} \\ \hline  & \text{Cozumel Island, Caribbean Sea} & \text{13–49} & \text{1–29} & \text{1} \\ \hline  & \text{Martinique, Caribbean Sea} & \text{37} & \text{23–26} & \text{<1} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

4.  Based on the data given in Table 7, decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 6 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{A decline in coral populations is observed throughout the whole distribution region of corals.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{The corals of the Great Barrier Reef are threatened by several environmental factors.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{The greatest threat is to the coral populations of the African coast.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{At least 3 years are needed to destroy a coral population completely.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{The coral stands of the Central American coast are threatened mainly by cyclones.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{All the factors threatening corals described in the table are able to destroy a coral population completely.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

The crown-of-thorns starfish (Acanthaster planci) is one of the largest starfish (Figure 34). The diameter of an adult individual is 30-70 cm. Unlike many other starfish, it is covered with poisonous spines 2-3 cm long. Like other starfish, it feeds by everting its stomach and covering the food. The crown-of-thorns starfish feeds only on corals; in a day it can dissolve and absorb up to 500 cm2 of coral, leaving only the shells.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig34.png

Figure 34. Crown-of-thorns starfish (Acanthaster planci).

Fossil evidence shows that corals and crown-of-thorns starfish have coexisted for several million years. Figure 35 shows the fluctuations of the coral and starfish populations.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig35.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): Koraļļu un ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigznes relatīvais skaits → Relative number of corals and crown-of-thorns starfish; Gads → Year

Figure 35. Fluctuations of the populations of corals and crown-of-thorns starfish.

5.  Answer the questions! [1 point for each correct answer; 4 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Curve No. 1 in Figure 35 corresponds to:} & \text{a. the crown-of-thorns starfish population;; b. the coral population.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{The curves shown in Figure 35 correspond to the following type of population fluctuation:} & \text{a. predator and prey;; b. host and parasite;; c. competition;; d. symbiotic relationships.} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{What role do organisms play that significantly change the overall structure of a population (for example, the crown-of-thorns starfish in a coral population)?} & \text{a. Help to maintain species diversity in the ecosystem.; b. Degrade the environment until it is no longer suitable for living.; c. Serve as a food base for autotrophic organisms.; d. problems.problem_orig:
N2016-11-4. Apdraudētās koraļļu populācijas

1.  Iepazīsties ar tekstu! Izvēlies pareizos jēdzienus. [1 p. par katru pareizo atbildi; 9 p.]

Koraļļi ir koloniāli organismi, kas sastāv daudziem ģenētiski identiskiem <divdīgļlapjiem | plakantārpiem | vēžveidīgajiem | zarndobumaiņiem>. Katram koraļļa indivīdu aptver ciets <CaCl2 | CaCO3 | Fe2O3 | SiO2> apvalks. Koraļļi spēj vairoties gan dzimumiski, gan bezdzimumiski. Vairojoties <bezdzimumiski | dzimumiski>, koraļļa "zara" galā esošie organismi pumpurojas un no tā noraisās jauns ģenētiski identisks organisms. <Bezdzimumiskas | dzimumiskas> vairošanās gadījumā koraļļi ūdenī izdala spermatozoīdus un olšūnas. Apaugļojoties olšūnai, rodas peldošs organisms, kas spēj radīt jaunu koraļļu koloniju. Daudzi koloniālie koraļļi veido koraļļu audzes, ko parasti dēvē par <bērnudārzu | mežiem | pulkiem | rifiem>. Tajos ir <augsta | niecīga | zema> bioloģiskā daudzveidība, tādēļ tie ir aizsargājamas teritorijas. Visvairāk koraļļu audzes ir sastopamas <arktiskajā | atlantiskajā | mērenajā | tropu un subtropu> klimatiskajā zonā.

Nesen presē parādījās ziņas, ka Lielais Barjerrifs ir pasludināts par mirušu. Šādas ziņas pamatā bija atklājumi par “koraļļu izbalēšanu”. Kolonijās dzīvojošajiem koraļļiem iekšējo šūnu slānī dzīvo simbiotiskas aļģes. Simbiotiskās aļģes korallim piegādā <minerālvielas | neorganiskās vielas | organiskās vielas>, ko tās saražo ar <elpošanas | filtrācijas | fotosintēzes> palīdzību. Naktīs korallis atritina taustekļus un ķer planktonu. Daļa planktonā esošo barības vielu tiek atdota simbiotiskām aļģēm. Krāsu korallim piešķir aļģu pigmenti. Nelabvēlīgu apstākļu ietekmē simbiotiskās aļģes no koraļļa pazūd un tas kļūst balts, tādēļ šo parādību sauc par “koraļļu izbalēšanu”. Nelabvēlīgie apstākļi, kas var izraisīt “koraļļu izbalēšanu”, ir paaugstināta ūdens temperatūra, ķīmiskais piesārņojums un infekcijas. Ja nelabvēlīgie apstākļi ir īslaicīgi, korallis spēj atgūt simbiotiskās aļģes. Ilgstoši bez simbiotiskajām aļģēm korallis dzīvot nespēj un iet bojā.

2.  Novērtē apgalvojumu patiesumu (P – patiess; A - aplams)! [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 4 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Apgalvojums} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Koraļļu audzes ir sastopamas tikai seklā ūdenī, kur tās spēj sasniegt saules gaisma.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Plaša koraļļu balēšana ir novērojama gados, kuros ir izteikts El Ninjo.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Kolonijas veidojošajiem koraļļiem simbiotiskās aļģes nav nepieciešamas dzīvības procesu uzturēšanai.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Lielais Barjerrifs nav pakļauts koraļļu izbalēšanai.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Zinātnieki vēlējās novērtēt ieguvumu, kādu korallim sniedz simbiotiskās aļģes. Šādā nolūkā ūdens tika piesātināts ar iezīmētu $\mathrm{CO_2}$, un tika izsekota oglekļa plūsma korallī. Pētījumā iegūtie rezultāti redzami 33. attēlā.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig33.png

33. att. Oglekļa plūsma korallī, ar skaitli norādīts iezīmētā oglekļa daudzums miligramos.

3.  Novērtē apgalvojumu patiesumu (P – patiess; A - aplams)! [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 6 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Apgalvojums} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Bez simbiotiskajām aļģēm koraļļi nespēj iegūt oglekli.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Gan korallis, gan simbiotiskās aļģes augšanas procesiem atvēl mazāk nekā 1\% uzņemtā oglekļa.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Aļģes un korallis elpošanai tērē vienādu daļu uzņemtā oglekļa.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Elpošanas procesā ogleklis organismu atstāj }\mathrm{CO_2}\text{ formā.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Organismi elpo, lai uzņemtās barības vielas pārveidotu par enerģiju.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Koraļļu lēno augšanu var izskaidrot ar tā oglekļa bilanci.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Koraļļu audzes apdraud ne tikai koraļļu izbalēšana, bet arī citi faktori, piemēram, cikloni un plēsīgu jūraszvaigžņu savairošanās. 7. tabulā ir apkopoti vairāku pētījumu rezultāti par dažādu kaitīgo faktoru ietekmi uz koraļļu populācijām.

7. tab. Koraļļu populācijas dažādās ģeogrāfiskās vietās pirms un pēc koraļļus apdraudošo faktoru iedarbības.

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Bojājumu veids} & \text{Vieta} & \text{Koraļļu segums pirms bojājumiem, \%} & \text{Koraļļu segums pēc bojājumiem, \%} & \text{Novērojumu ilgums, gadi} \\ \hline \text{Koraļļu izbalēšana} & \text{Arābijas līcis} & \text{90} & \text{22–26} & \text{3} \\ \hline  & \text{Kenijas piekraste} & \text{26} & \text{23} & \text{5} \\ \hline  & \text{Tanzānijas piekraste} & \text{33} & \text{0–3} & \text{6} \\ \hline  & \text{Seišeļu salas} & \text{29–64} & \text{0–10} & \text{1} \\ \hline  & \text{Čagas salas, Indijas okeāns} & \text{25–35} & \text{7–33} & \text{8} \\ \hline  & \text{Japāna} & \text{95} & \text{0} & \text{2} \\ \hline  & \text{Lielais Barjerrifs, Austrālija} & \text{39–63} & \text{9–45} & \text{<1} \\ \hline \text{Ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigznes (Acanthaster planci) savairošanās} & \text{Japāna} & \text{80} & \text{0} & \text{2} \\ \hline  & \text{Samoa salas, Klusais okeāns} & \text{70} & \text{57} & \text{9} \\ \hline  & \text{Franču Polinēzija, Klusais okeāns} & \text{36} & \text{20} & \text{1} \\ \hline \text{Ciklons} & \text{Lielais Barjerrifs, Austrālija} & \text{85} & \text{5} & \text{4} \\ \hline  & \text{Tuvalu salas, Klusais okeāns} & \text{4–93} & \text{1–54} & \text{3} \\ \hline  & \text{Kozumela sala, Karību jūra} & \text{13–49} & \text{1–29} & \text{1} \\ \hline  & \text{Martinika, Karību jūra} & \text{37} & \text{23–26} & \text{<1} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

4.  Balstoties uz 7. tabulā dotajiem datiem, novērtē apgalvojumu patiesumu (P – patiess; A - aplams)! [1 p. par katru pareizu atbildi; 6 p.]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Apgalvojums} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Koraļļu populāciju samazināšanās ir novērojama visā koraļļu izplatības reģionā.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Lielā Barjerrifa koraļļus apdraud vairāki vides faktori.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Lielākais apdraudējums ir Āfrikas piekrastes koraļļu populācijām.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Lai koraļļu populāciju iznīcinātu pilnīgi, ir nepieciešami vismaz 3 gadi.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Centrālamerikas piekrastes koraļļu audzes apdraud pārsvarā cikloni.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Visi tabulā raksturotie koraļļus apdraudošie faktori spēj pilnīgi iznīcināt koraļļu populāciju.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigzne (Acanthaster planci) ir viena no lielākajām jūraszvaigznēm (34. attēls). Pieauguša īpatņa diametrs ir 30-70 cm. Atšķirībā no daudzām citām jūraszvaigznēm, tā ir klāta ar 2-3 cm gariem, indīgiem ērkšķiem. Tāpat kā citas jūraszvaigznes tā barojas, izvēršot kuņģi uz āru un apklājot barību. Ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigzne barojas tikai ar koraļļiem, dienā tā spēj izšķīdināt un absorbēt līdz pat 500 cm2 koraļļu, atstājot tikai čaulas.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig34.png

34. att. Ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigzne (Acanthaster planci).

Fosilie pierādījumi liecina, ka koraļļi un ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigznes ir sadzīvojuši jau vairākus miljonus gadus. 35. attēlā redzamas koraļļu un jūras zvaigznes populāciju svārstības.

35. att. Koraļļu un ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigžņu populāciju svārstības.

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Jautājums} & \text{Izvēlies pareizo atbildi!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{35. attēlā līknei Nr. 1 atbilst:} & \text{a. ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigznes populācija;; b. koraļļu populācija.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{35. attēlā redzamās līknes atbilst šādam populāciju svārstību veidam:} & \text{a. plēsējs un upuris;; b. saimnieks un parazīts;; c. konkurence;; d. simbiotiskas attiecības.} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Kādu lomu pilda organismi, kas būtiski maina kopējo populācijas struktūru (piemēram, ērkšķu kroņa jūraszvaigzne koraļļu populācijā)?} & \text{a. Palīdz saglabāt sugu daudzveidību ekosistēmā.; b. Degradē vidi, līdz tā vairs nav piemērota dzīvošanai.; c. Kalpo par barības bāzi autotrofiem organismiem.; d. Ir barības ķēdes pamata līmenī.} \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Kāpēc koraļļu rifi šobrīd ir īpaši apdraudēti?} & \text{a. Koraļļi tiek pastiprināti izmantoti kosmētikas rūpniecībā.; b. problems.problem:
N2016-11-5. Cell organelles and genetic diseases

1.  Study the diagram of the cross-sectional structure of a cell shown in Figure 36. In the table write the label of the corresponding cell organelle in the figure. [1 point for each correct answer; 10 points]

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig36.png

Figure 36. Schematic cross-section of a cell.

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Organelle} & \text{Label in Fig. 36} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Nucleolus} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Nucleus} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Ribosome} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{Rough endoplasmic reticulum} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Golgi complex} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{Smooth endoplasmic reticulum} &  \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{Mitochondrion} &  \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{Cytoplasm} &  \\ \hline \text{9.} & \text{Centrosome} &  \\ \hline \text{10.} & \text{Cell membrane} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

2.  Decide whether each statement is true (P – patiess) or false (A – aplams)! [1 point for each correct answer; 10 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|c|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Statement} & \text{P/A} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Oxygen crosses the cell membrane freely.} &  \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{All cell structures that are not surrounded by membranes, for example glucagon granules, centrioles, proteasomes, are called inclusions.} &  \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Ribosomes that are attached to other organelles are called fixed ribosomes, and those that are located freely in the cytosol are called free ribosomes.} &  \\ \hline \text{4.} & \text{The cytoskeleton in the cell has three basic functions: support, movement and signalling.} &  \\ \hline \text{5.} & \text{Synthesis of proteins, fatty acids and lipids takes place in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, and there they are also modified for further use in the cell.} &  \\ \hline \text{6.} & \text{For a molecule to reach the mitochondrial matrix, it must cross the outer mitochondrial membrane, the intermembrane space and the inner membrane.} &  \\ \hline \text{7.} & \text{In specialised cells of the organism some of the functions of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum are the synthesis of steroid hormones, the deactivation of medicines and the storage of }\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\text{ ions.} &  \\ \hline \text{8.} & \text{Lysosomes contain enzymes that can break down bacteria and aged organelles.} &  \\ \hline \text{9.} & \text{The centrosome and the lysosome are surrounded by the cell membrane.} &  \\ \hline \text{10.} & \text{Some of the functions of the cell membrane are the barrier function, the exchange of substances with the environment and the support function.} &  \\ \hline \end{array}$$

The following tasks describe four diseases whose pathogenesis is related to damage to particular cell organelles. Read the description of the disease and deduce damage to which cell organelle underlies the disease.

Progeria is a rare autosomal dominant disease in which a person ages prematurely. This hereditary disease is caused by a mutation in the LMNA gene, whose product is lamin A. The defective (truncated) lamin A is called progerin. Lamin is involved in the formation of the nucleus in cells. Figure 37 shows a child with progeria, as well as the nucleus of a cell of a healthy person and of a progeria patient.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig37.png

Figure 37. A child with progeria and the cell nucleus in a cell of a healthy person (A) and of a progeria patient (B).

Skin fibroblasts of progeria patients and of healthy people were stained with fluorescently labelled antibodies that bind to certain cell proteins. The results of this experiment are shown in Figure 38.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig38.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): lamīns A/progerīns → lamin A/progerin; mikrocaurulītes → microtubules; + DNS → + DNA; progerija → progeria; norma → normal

Figure 38. Fibroblasts of healthy people and of progeria patients in metaphase. The first column shows images with stained lamin A/progerin, the 2nd column with stained microtubules; in the 3rd column the staining of both proteins is combined and DNA is stained (in blue).

3.  Study Figures 37 and 38 and answer the questions! [1 point for each correct answer; 2 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{In the case of progeria there are:} & \text{a. defects of the nucleolus;; b. defects of the nuclear membrane;; c. defects of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane;; d. a lack of the protein forming the nuclear pore.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Why is accelerated ageing observed in progeria?} & \text{a. Because of impaired nuclear division, cell division occurs less frequently.; b. There are disturbances of DNA synthesis in the cells.; c. Because nuclear pores are lacking, the raw materials for DNA synthesis do not enter the nucleus.; d. Dysfunction of the endoplasmic reticulum membranes associated with the nuclear membranes causes secondary disturbances in the functioning of the nucleus.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Type II mucolipidosis (I-cell disease, or inclusion cell disease) is a lysosomal storage disease. This disease is associated with defects in the “maturation” of lysosomal enzymes (hydrolases) in the cell after their translation. A typical hydrolase is a glycoprotein – a protein with residues of sugars, for example mannose, on its surface. Some of the mannose residues may be phosphorylated; such phosphorylation is carried out by the enzymes glucosaminyl phosphotransferases. Mannose-6-phosphate groups on the protein surface are tags that allow the receptors on the surface of lysosomal membranes to recognise hydrolases so that these enzymes reach their site of action. In I-cell disease a defect has arisen in the enzyme that transfers the phosphate group to mannose residues. If there is no phosphorylated mannose residue on the surface of the hydrolase, it does not reach the lysosome but remains in the vesicle and, together with the other secretory vesicles of the Golgi complex, is secreted from the cell.

4.  Answer the questions! [1 point for each correct answer; 2 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{What happens in the cells of patients with I-cell disease?} & \text{a. The cells contain many large lysosomes. Because the lysosomes lack enzymes that would break down the substances that have got into them, the undegraded substances accumulate in the lysosomes, while lysosomes accumulate in the cells.; b. The cells lack lysosomes. Because there are no lysosomal enzymes, lysosomes do not form at all.; c. The cells contain many small lysosomes that have no contents because enzymes are lacking.; d. The cell contains one large lysosome, also called a megaphagosome. The undegraded substances accumulate in the cytoplasm.} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Where are the non-functioning lysosomal enzymes found in large amounts in patients with I-cell disease?} & \text{a. In small lysosomes that contain only non-functioning enzymes. These lysosomes cannot take up substances to be broken down because they are defective.; b. They cannot be found anywhere. The non-functioning enzymes are broken down in the cells, and the resulting amino acids are used again in the cell’s metabolism.; c. In the blood, because they are secreted outside the cells. In a patient’s blood sample the lysosomal level can be even 20 times higher than in healthy people.; d. In the lysosomes together with the substances to be broken down. The defect of the hydrolases does not allow the substances to be broken down, therefore they accumulate together with the defective enzymes.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Pyruvic acid (pyruvate dehydrogenase, PDH) complex deficiency is an inherited neurodegenerative disease associated with carbohydrate metabolism. PDH converts pyruvate into acetyl-coenzyme A, which is involved in the tricarboxylic acid or Krebs cycle. The Krebs cycle is a cycle of biochemical reactions that allows energy to be obtained from carbohydrates, therefore disturbances of this cycle manifest as a lack of energy in the body. A diagram describing the obtaining of energy in the cell is shown in Figure 39.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig39.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): Glikolīze → Glycolysis; Pienskābe → Lactic acid; Taukskābes → Fatty acids; Glikoze → Glucose; Pirovīnogskābe → Pyruvic acid; Acetil-koenzīms A → Acetyl-coenzyme A; Krebsa cikls → Krebs cycle; Tiamīns → Thiamine; Glikoneoģenēze → Gluconeogenesis

Figure 39. Energy metabolism in the cell. PDH – pyruvate dehydrogenase; DCA – dichloroacetate.

5.  Study the diagram and answer the questions! [1 point for each correct answer; 3 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{The level of which compound in the cell will be raised in the case of PDH complex deficiency?} & \text{a. Thiamine; b. Acetyl-coenzyme A; c. Lactic acid; d. Pyruvic acid} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Which substances should a patient with PDG complex deficiency take in increased amounts in order to promote energy uptake in the cell?} & \text{a. Carbohydrates; b. Fatty acids; c. Thiamine; d. Glucose} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{Where in the cell is PDH located?} & \text{a. In the cell nucleus; b. In the mitochondria; c. In the endoplasmic reticulum; d. In the Golgi complex} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Bridges–Good syndrome, or chronic granulomatous disease, is a group of inherited immune system diseases in which reactive oxygen radicals are not formed in the peroxisomes of phagocytes. These compounds are needed for the death of the pathogens that have been taken up after their phagocytosis. In this disease the immune system is usually able to fight bacteria that do not contain catalase, but cannot bring about the death of catalase-positive bacteria. Catalase is an enzyme that splits hydrogen peroxide – one of the oxygen compounds that immune system cells use to kill microorganisms. Bacteria that synthesise catalase break down the hydrogen peroxide produced in the peroxisomes.

The catalase test is performed to find out whether a bacterium contains catalase. A drop of hydrogen peroxide is applied to a microscope slide, and a sample of the bacterial culture is added to it. A culture of Enterococcus spp. bacteria was applied to slide A, and a culture of Staphylococcus aureus to slide B (Figure 40).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig40.png

Figure 40. Catalase test with a culture of enterococcus (A) and of golden staphylococcus (B).

The yellow dye nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT), in turn, is used to diagnose chronic granulomatous disease. If oxygen radicals are not formed in phagocytes, they cannot reduce NBT to the insoluble blue compound formazan. The NBT test was performed in the samples of two patients (A and B), and the results of the test are shown in Figure 41.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig41.png

Figure 41. NBT test in the samples of two patients (A and B).

6.  Answer the questions about catalase and granulomatosis! [1 point for each correct answer; 3 points]

$$\begin{array}{|c|l|l|}\hline \text{\#} & \text{Question} & \text{Choose the correct answer!} \\ \hline \text{1.} & \text{Which bacteria synthesise catalase?} & \text{a. Staphylococcus; b. Enterococcus} \\ \hline \text{2.} & \text{Against which of these bacteria are the immune system cells of a patient with chronic granulomatosis unable to fight?} & \text{a. Staphylococcus; b. Enterococcus} \\ \hline \text{3.} & \text{The cells of a patient with chronic granulomatosis are seen in Figure 41:} & \text{a. in part A;; b. in part B.} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

N2016-11-5. Šūnas organoīdi un ģenētiskās slimības
