V2017-11/12-2. Metabolism and adipose tissue

Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions in an organism. Biosynthetic reactions, during which complex compounds are formed from simple compounds and chemical ATP energy is consumed, are collectively called plastic metabolism, or anabolism. In energy metabolism, on the other hand, simple compounds are formed from complex compounds and energy is released during these reactions. Reactions of this type are collectively also called catabolism. All those processes that result in the formation of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) are a component of energy metabolism. The energy metabolism of an individual can be characterised by the metabolic rate (MR), which is expressed as the amount of energy consumed per unit of time (usually per day). Traditionally the metabolic rate is expressed in kilocalories per day (kcal/day).

1.  Complete the tasks on the basic concepts of metabolism! [7 points]

1.  Name an example of an anabolic reaction in an animal organism!

2.  Name an example of a catabolic reaction in an animal organism!

3.  Metabolic reactions in which ATP is formed and which take place in the presence of oxygen are called: ____ reactions

4.  Metabolic reactions in which ATP is formed and which take place under oxygen-free conditions are called: ____ reactions

5.  What is a kilocalorie?

6.  Write in the scheme the factors that can affect the metabolic rate of an individual!

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-2017-2-2-x1.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): Vielmaiņas intensitāte → Metabolic rate

As a result of a reduced metabolic rate, additional adipose tissue may form in the body and fat accumulation may occur. The simplest method for assessing whether excessive accumulation of adipose tissue is occurring is the calculation of the body mass index (BMI, $\mathrm{kg/m^2}$). The body mass assessment scale recognised by the World Health Organization is shown in Table 10.

Table 10. Body mass assessment scale (WHO).

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|}\hline \text{Body mass category} & \text{BMI, kg/m}^2 \\ \hline \text{Underweight} & <18.5 \\ \hline \text{Normal body mass} & 18.5\text{-}24.9 \\ \hline \text{Excess body mass (overweight)} & 25.0\text{-}29.9 \\ \hline \text{Grade 1 obesity} & 30.0\text{-}34.9 \\ \hline \text{Grade 2 obesity} & 35.0\text{-}39.9 \\ \hline \text{Grade 3 obesity} & \geq 40 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

2.  Alice’s body mass is 73 kg and her height is 165 cm. Complete the tasks on fat accumulation and Alice’s BMI! [3.5 points]

1.  Name four more factors, besides a reduced metabolic rate, that can promote the formation of adipose tissue!

2.  Calculate Alice’s BMI! ____ $\mathrm{kg/m^2}$

3.  Draw conclusions about Alice’s body mass category and whether action is needed in her case to control body mass!

Figure 63 shows the main sites of adipose tissue accumulation under the skin and around the abdominal cavity organs (subcutaneous and visceral adipose tissue, respectively). The fat that accumulates around the abdominal cavity organs is the most harmful to health, so in the clinic it is important to assess not only the total amount of body fat but also the amount of visceral adipose tissue.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/lvbo-fig63.png

Figure labels (Latvian → English): taukainā akna → omentum; retroperitoneālie tauki → retroperitoneal fat; aizkuņģa dziedzeris → pancreas; perirenālie tauki → perirenal fat; zarnas → intestines; mezentērija tauki → mesenteric fat; gluteālie zemādas tauki → gluteal subcutaneous fat; femorālie zemādas tauki → femoral subcutaneous fat; preperitoneālie → preperitoneal; kuņģis → stomach; zemādas tauki (virsējie) → subcutaneous fat (superficial); zemādas tauki (dziļie) → subcutaneous fat (deep); tauku plēves tauki → fat of the fascia

Figure 63. Main sites of adipose tissue accumulation under the skin and around the visceral organs.

3.  Examination methods are named below that can be used to assess the amount of adipose tissue in different parts of the body. Study the list of methods and complete the tasks! [3.5 points]

V2017-11-3. Twin studies and heritability

Why do relatives have similar traits, and why do they more often suffer from the same diseases? The similarity of traits within one family can be explained both by shared genes and by a shared environment. To discover the factors that determine the appearance of a trait or disease, researchers use various methods, and one of them is twin studies. Twin studies compare how often a trait is or is not observed in twins. These studies compare the concordance of a trait between monozygotic (MZ) twins and dizygotic (MZ) twins.

1.  Answer the questions about twins and shared environmental factors! [3 points]

1.  What proportion of genes is shared by monozygotic twins (MZ)? ____%

2.  What proportion of genes is shared by dizygotic twins (DZ)? ____%

3.  Mark all those environmental factors that are shared by a family living together!

[ ] Socio-economic status.

[ ] Intrauterine environment and the course of birth.

[ ] Dietary habits.

[ ] Air pollution.

[ ] X chromosome inactivation in female cells.

[ ] Medications used to treat a disease.

Heritability is a quantity that describes how great the importance of the action of genes is in the development of a trait, as opposed to the effect of environmental factors. Heritability is denoted by $h^2$, and the value of this quantity can vary in the range from 0 (all phenotypic variability is determined by external environmental factors) to 1 (phenotypic variability is determined only by genes). Heritability is calculated using the following formula:

$$h^2 = \frac{\text{variability in DZ pairs} - \text{variability in MZ pairs}}{\text{variability in DZ pairs}}$$

problems.problem:
V2017-12-3. The ability to taste bitter taste

The ability to taste a bitter taste has been linked in the human genome to more than 28 different genes. Because dangerous substances and poisonous plants are often bitter, the ability to taste bitter substances is a selective advantage.

The ability to taste the bitter compound phenylthiocarbamide is determined by the PTC gene. People who can taste phenylthiocarbamide are called tasters, and these people have the dominant allele (F) of the PTC gene. In people who are homozygous for the dominant allele, phenylthiocarbamide causes a strong sensation of bitter taste, while heterozygotes describe it as a somewhat bitter taste. People for whom phenylthiocarbamide does not cause a taste sensation are called non-tasters, and in them the recessive allele of PTC is in the homozygous state (ff).

Thiourea is also a bitter substance, but the ability to taste it is determined by a different gene. Tasters of phenylthiocarbamide are often also able to taste thiourea, but this association is not observed in all cases. The ability to taste thiourea is a dominant trait (T), while not tasting thiourea is recessive (tt).

The bitter taste threshold can be determined by tasting solutions containing quinine in various dilutions. The different sensitivity to quinine is determined by the alleles of the TAS2R19 gene – H2, H1 and h. The H2 allele determines high sensitivity, H1 – medium sensitivity, h is a recessive allele, and individuals homozygous for h (hh) cannot taste quinine. The higher the dilution at which someone can perceive the bitter taste of quinine, the more pronounced the perception of bitter taste. People homozygous for the H1 allele have a higher sensitivity to the bitter taste of quinine than people who are heterozygous for the H2 and h alleles.

Coriander is a widely used spice that seems somewhat bitter or sweet to a large proportion of people. However, about 11% of people describe the taste of coriander as “soapy” and unpleasant. Liking or disliking the taste of coriander is determined by three genes. The dominant allele (G) of the GNAT3 gene, i.e. the gustducin gene, determines the occurrence of a taste sensation when eating coriander. The perception of the bitter taste of coriander is determined by the dominant allele (K) of the receptor TAS2R50, while individuals homozygous for the recessive allele (kk) taste coriander as sweet. The dominant allele (Z) of the TRPA1 gene is responsible for tasting the unpleasant, soap-like taste.

Depending on the interaction of the bitter taste genes, some people are so-called supertasters. Supertasters not only can taste bitter taste, but their perception of bitter taste is especially pronounced and not only grapefruit but also, for example, broccoli, Brussels sprouts and kale seem bitter to them. Individuals who can taste the 4th and 5th dilutions of quinine are considered supertasters.

In studying people’s ability to taste bitter substances, scientists have concluded that there is a relationship between taste peculiarities and food choices. Supertasters are especially sensitive to nuances of bitter taste in all foods. To balance the bitter taste, they tend to intensify other taste sensations by adding more flavourings – sugar, pepper, salt.

You have arrived on a small island, Rengu, and ask 10 local young people to taste four substances and to answer the question of how, in their opinion, these substances taste. The answers given by the young people are summarised in the table below!

problems.problem_orig:
V2017-12-3. Spēja sagaršot rūgto garšu

Spēja sagaršot rūgtu garšu cilvēka genomā ir tikusi saistīta ar vairāk nekā 28 dažādiem gēniem. Tā kā bīstamas vielas un indīgi augi bieži vien ir rūgti, spējai sagaršot rūgtas vielas ir selektīva priekšrocība.

Spēju sagaršot rūgtu savienojumu feniltiokarbamīdu nosaka gēns PTC. Cilvēki, kas spēj sagaršot feniltiokarbamīdu, tiek saukti par sagaršotājiem, un šiem cilvēkiem ir PTC gēna dominantā alēle (F). Cilvēkiem, kas ir homozigotiski pēc dominantās alēles, feniltiokarbamīds izraisa stipru rūgtās garšas sajūtu, heterozigoti to raksturo kā rūgtenu garšu. Cilvēki, kuriem feniltiokarbamīds neizraisa garšas sajūtu, tiek saukti par nesagaršotāji, un tiem PTC recesīvā alēle ir homozigotiskā stāvoklī (ff).

Arī tiourīnviela ir rūgta viela, taču spēju to sagaršot nosaka cits gēns. Feniltiokarbamīda sagaršotāji bieži spēj sagaršot arī tiourīnvielu, tomēr šī saistība nav novērojama visos gadījumos. Spēja sagaršot tiourīnvielu ir dominanta pazīme (T), savukārt tiourīnvielas nesagaršošana – recesīva (tt).

Rūgtās garšas slieksni var noteikt, pagaršojot šķīdumus, kas satur hinīnu dažādos atšķaidījumos. Atšķirīgo jutību pret hinīnu nosaka TAS2R19 gēna alēles – H2, H1 un h. H2 alēle nosaka augstu jutību, H1 – vidēju jutību, h ir recesīva alēle un pēc h homozigotiski indivīdi (hh) hinīnu nesagaršo. Jo lielākā atšķaidījuma pakāpē kāds spēj sajust hinīna rūgto garšu, jo izteiktāka ir rūgtās garšas uztvere. Pēc H1 alēles homozigotiskiem cilvēkiem ir augstāka jutība pret hinīna rūgto garšu nekā cilvēkiem, kas ir heterozigotiski pēc H2 un h alēles.

Koriandrs ir plaši lietota garšviela, kas lielai daļai cilvēku šķiet rūgtena vai salda. Tomēr aptuveni 11% cilvēku koriandra garšu raksturo kā “ziepjainu” un nepatīkamu. Patiku vai nepatiku pret koriandra garšu nosaka trīs gēni. GNAT3 jeb gustducīna gēna dominantā alēle (G) nosaka garšas sajūtas rašanos, ēdot koriandru. Koriandra rūgtās garšas uztveri nosaka receptora TAS2R50 dominantā alēle (K), bet indivīdi, kas homozigotiski pēc recesīvās alēles (kk), koriandru sagaršo kā saldu. TRPA1 gēna dominantā alēle (Z) ir atbildīga par nepatīkamās, ziepēm līdzīgās garšas sagaršošanu.

Atkarībā no rūgtās garšas gēnu mijiedarbības daži cilvēki ir tā saucamie supersagaršotāji. Supersagaršotāji ne tikai spēj sagaršot rūgtu garšu, bet viņiem rūgtās garšas uztvere ir īpaši izteikta un rūgti šķiet ne tikai greipfrūti, bet arī, piemēram, brokoļi, Briseles kāposti un lapu kāposti. Par supersagaršotājiem uzskata tos indivīdus, kas spēj sagaršot hinīna 4. un 5. atšķaidījumu.

Pētot cilvēku spēju sagaršot rūgtās vielas, zinātnieki ir secinājuši, ka pastāv sakarība starp garšas īpatnībām un ēdienu izvēli. Supersagaršotāji ir īpaši jutīgi pret rūgtās garšas niansēm visos ēdienos. Lai līdzsvarotu rūgto garšu, viņiem ir tendence citas garšas sajūtas pastiprināt, pievienojot vairāk garšvielu – cukuru, piparus, sāli.

Tu esi ieradies uz nelielas salas Rengu un lūdz 10 vietējos jauniešus pagaršot četras vielas un atbildēt uz jautājumu, kā šīs vielas viņuprāt garšo. Jauniešu sniegtās atbildes ir apkopotas tabulā zemāk!

25.  African swine fever (ĀCM; Pestis africana suum) is a highly contagious, acute infectious disease of pigs with a high mortality. Originally the disease occurred in Africa, South America and the Caribbean countries, but in Europe it was first recorded in 1957 in Portugal, then in Spain, France and Italy. At present it has been present permanently and for many years in Sardinia. In Latvia ĀCM was first recorded on 26 June 2014. Only animals of the pig family (Suidae) fall ill: domestic pigs, wild boars and wild-living pigs of other species. ĀCM can acquire an endemic character if the ĀCM virus has entered the population of wild boars and other wild-living pig species of the pig family and arthropods – ticks (Ornithodorus spp). ĀCM spreads in the pig population through direct or indirect contact. ĀCM does not respond to medicinal treatment, and no effective vaccine is available for the prevention of this disease. The ĀCM virus is very resistant – in the external environment it persists for at least 11 days in faeces (manure) at ambient temperature and for at least 1 month in a contaminated (infected) pigsty. The ĀCM virus can be present in all tissues of the animal, but in a high concentration the virus is always in the liquid tissue of the organism – the blood (information from the website of the Ministry of Agriculture).

1. One of the symptoms in sick pigs is bloody diarrhoea, which promotes the spread of the virus in the wild. (P/A)

Sākotnēji slimība bija sastopama Āfrikā, Dienvidamerikā un Karību jūras valstīs, bet Eiropā tā pirmo reizi reģistrēta 1957. gadā Portugālē, pēc tam - Spānijā, Francijā, Itālijā. Pašlaik pastāvīgi un daudzus gadus tā sastopama Sardīnijā. Latvijā ĀCM pirmo reizi reģistrēts 2014. gada 26. jūnijā. Slimo tikai cūku dzimtas dzīvnieki (Suidae): mājas, meža un savvaļā mītošas citu sugu cūkas. 26.  African swine fever (ASF; Latvian abbreviation ĀCM) (Pestis africana suum) is a highly contagious, acute infectious disease of pigs with a high mortality. Originally the disease occurred in Africa, South America and the countries of the Caribbean, but in Europe it was first registered in 1957 in Portugal, then in Spain, France and Italy. At present it has been present continuously for many years in Sardinia. In Latvia ASF was first registered on 26 June 2014. Only animals of the pig family (Suidae) get ill: domestic pigs, wild boars and wild-living pigs of other species. ASF can become endemic if the ASF virus has entered the population of wild boars and other wild-living pig species of the pig family and arthropods – ticks (Ornithodorus spp). ASF spreads in the pig population through direct or indirect contact. ASF does not respond to drug treatment, and no effective vaccine for the prevention of this disease is available. The ASF virus is very resistant – in the external environment it survives for at least 11 days in faeces (manure) at ambient temperature and for at least 1 month in a contaminated (infected) pig pen. The ASF virus can be present in all tissues of the animal, but in high concentration the virus is always present in the liquid tissues of the body – the blood (information from the website of the Ministry of Agriculture).

2. Because ASF has a high mortality and no medicines for treating this disease are available, quarantine measures must be observed in order to avoid a widespread ASF epidemic. (P/A)

3. ASF could theoretically be treated with antibiotics. (P/A)

28.  Citrus fruits have a complex evolutionary history. Genetic studies have concluded that all citrus fruits are based on four species – citron (Citrus medica), pomelo (C. maxima), mandarin (C. reticulata) and papeda (C. micrantha, "bitter lemon"). The region of origin for citrons is northern Indochina, for pomelo – Malaysia, for mandarins – Vietnam and southern China, and for papeda – Japan. All four species are able to form hybrids with one another. Oranges are a hybrid of mandarin and pomelo, and genetic analyses show that 25% of the genes of an orange have come from pomelo and 75% from mandarin. By crossing an orange with a pomelo, the grapefruit was obtained.

2. Oranges were created by crossing mandarin with pomelo and propagating the resulting F1 offspring further only vegetatively. (P/A)

3. Pomelos, citrons, mandarins and papedas most likely descend from one ancestor, and the formation of these species was influenced by geographic isolation. (P/A)

4. Wild citrus plants can be used to introduce genes that provide resistance to various diseases into already established citrus varieties. (P/A)

29.  African swine fever (ASF; Latvian abbreviation ĀCM) (Pestis africana suum) is a highly contagious, acute infectious disease of pigs with a high mortality. Originally the disease occurred in Africa, South America and the countries of the Caribbean, but in Europe it was first registered in 1957 in Portugal, then in Spain, France and Italy. At present it has been present continuously for many years in Sardinia. In Latvia ASF was first registered on 26 June 2014. Only animals of the pig family (Suidae) get ill: domestic pigs, wild boars and wild-living pigs of other species. ASF can become endemic if the ASF virus has entered the population of wild boars and other wild-living pig species of the pig family and arthropods – ticks (Ornithodorus spp). ASF spreads in the pig population through direct or indirect contact. ASF does not respond to drug treatment, and no effective vaccine for the prevention of this disease is available. The ASF virus is very resistant – in the external environment it survives for at least 11 days in faeces (manure) at ambient temperature and for at least 1 month in a contaminated (infected) pig pen. The ASF virus can be present in all tissues of the animal, but in high concentration the virus is always present in the liquid tissues of the body – the blood (information from the website of the Ministry of Agriculture).

1. Because ASF has a high mortality and no medicines for treating this disease are available, quarantine measures must be observed in order to avoid a widespread ASF epidemic. (P/A)

2. ASF could theoretically be treated with antibiotics. (P/A)

3. The presence of the virus in meat can be determined using the polymerase chain reaction. (P/A)

4. Humans can fall ill with African swine fever. (P/A)

29.  Āfrikas cūku mēris (Pestis africana suum) ir ļoti lipīga, akūta cūku infekcijas slimība, kuras gadījumā ir augsta mirstība. Sākotnēji slimība bija sastopama Āfrikā, Dienvidamerikā un Karību jūras valstīs, bet Eiropā tā pirmo reizi reģistrēta 1957. gadā Portugālē, pēc tam - Spānijā, Francijā, Itālijā. Pašlaik pastāvīgi un daudzus gadus tā sastopama Sardīnijā. Latvijā ĀCM pirmo reizi reģistrēts 2014. gada 26. jūnijā. Slimo tikai cūku dzimtas dzīvnieki (Suidae): mājas, meža un savvaļā mītošas citu sugu cūkas. ĀCM var iegūt endēmisku raksturu, ja ĀCM vīruss ir iekļuvis meža cūku un citu cūku dzimtas savvaļā mītošu cūku sugu populācijā un posmkājos - ērcēs (Ornithodorus spp). ĀCM izplatās cūku populācijā ar tieša vai netieša kontakta starpniecību. ĀCM nepadodas medikamentozai ārstēšanai, un nav pieejama efektīva vakcīna šīs slimības profilaksei. ĀCM vīruss ir ļoti izturīgs – ārējā vidē tas saglabājas vismaz 11 dienas fēcēs (mēslos) apkārtējas vides temperatūrā un vismaz 1 mēnesi kontaminētā (inficētā) cūku aizgaldā. ĀCM vīruss var būt visos dzīvnieka audos, taču augstā koncentrācijā vīruss vienmēr ir šķidrajos organisma audos – asinīs (informācija no Zemkopības ministrijas mājaslapas).
